vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: structs-combat
Version: 1.1.0

The skill bundle contains metadata and a detailed markdown file describing combat operations for a game called 'Structs' using the `structsd` CLI tool. All commands and instructions are specific to the game's mechanics (e.g., `structsd tx structs struct-attack`, `planet-raid-compute`) and do not exhibit any signs of malicious intent, such as data exfiltration, unauthorized system access, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts against the AI agent. The instructions are purely functional for playing the game.

llm.summary: The skill's instructions match a combat/raid CLI guide for the Structs game, but it omits key dependency and credential declarations (it expects to sign transactions and run potentially long/CPU-heavy PoW compute), which is a meaningful coherence gap users should understand before running commands or giving access to keys.

dimensions.detail: The name and description describe combat/raid operations and the SKILL.md provides concrete structsd CLI commands that implement that purpose. However, the skill does not declare that it requires the structsd binary or a signing key infrastructure even though all runtime examples assume those are present.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to running structsd CLI transactions (scouting, stealth, attack, fleet-move, planet-raid-compute) and do not ask the agent to read unrelated files or exfiltrate data. They do instruct the user to run background PoW compute that may consume significant local CPU and to use --from [key-name], which implies access to local wallet keys.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec or code to write to disk, which minimizes install-time risk. The tradeoff: it assumes external tooling (structsd) exists but does not declare it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md repeatedly uses --from [key-name] to sign transactions, but the skill metadata lists no required credentials or primaryEnv. That mismatch means the skill implicitly requires access to signing keys (wallets) without declaring them. The work step (planet-raid-compute) also instructs prolonged local PoW hashing, which consumes resources but isn't declared as an operational requirement.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not always-enabled and has no install-time persistence or config changes. It does not request system-wide privileges in the metadata.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is a procedural guide for using the structsd CLI to attack, raid, and defend in a game. Before using it: (1) confirm you have the official structsd binary from a trusted source — the skill does not declare that dependency; (2) understand that commands use --from [key-name] and will sign on behalf of a wallet/key stored on your machine — do NOT use your main account: use a test or limited key with minimal funds/permissions; (3) planet-raid-compute runs a local Proof-of-Work that can run minutes to hours and will consume CPU — run on a machine you control and monitor resource usage; (4) verify legality and terms-of-service for any automated or hostile in-game actions you perform; (5) inspect and understand each structsd command before execution (there's no code sandbox here). The primary coherence issues are the missing declaration of the structsd dependency and the lack of an explicit credential requirement despite many transaction examples that will sign and submit transactions.
